title: croft.json
description: A croft project's configuration (croft docs config). Editors use this schema; croft checks croft.json itself, including what a schema cannot, such as whether the timezone is a real IANA zone.

$schema.description: this schema, so editors can check croft.json

database.description: the DuckDB file, relative to the project folder (absolute after relocation)

timezone.description: IANA zone for schedules, ::DATE and JSON timestamps, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles"; changing it rebuilds every transform

readCopy.description: keep warehouse.read.duckdb, a copy for GUIs and notebooks, refreshed after runs

serverMode.description: server mode: croft serve answers from a readers' process on the read copy (croft docs server-mode)

enabled.description: server mode: croft serve answers apps from a readers' process on the read copy and never opens the warehouse file; turns the read copy on, read-only on disk (croft docs server-mode)

acceptFullCopyCost.description: accept that every refresh of the read copy is a full copy of a warehouse over 1 GB (the filesystem cannot clone it); without this, server mode refuses to start there

quackHost.description: the address croft serve listens on for DuckDB 2.0 clients over Quack (croft docs quack); anything but loopback must sit behind an HTTPS reverse proxy

quackPort.description: the port for Quack; 0 picks a free one and the banner says which

quackPlaintextOnNetwork.description: accept that a quackHost other than loopback carries keys and queries in plaintext, behind an HTTPS reverse proxy of your own; without this croft serve refuses to start with such an address (ask the user first)

quackMaxConcurrent.description: Quack queries running at once, over all sessions; past it a query is refused with a retryable answer (1-64)

lake.description: lake mode: keep the warehouse in a DuckLake instead of the file. A shared lake is a Postgres catalog and an S3-compatible bucket; a local one (development) is a SQLite catalog and a folder (croft docs lake)

catalog.description: where the lake keeps its table list

kind.description: lake mode: keep the warehouse in a DuckLake. "postgres" is a shared lake (a Postgres catalog and a bucket); "sqlite" is a local one for development (croft docs lake)

host.description: the Postgres server that holds the lake's catalog, e.g. "db.example.com"

database.description: the Postgres database that holds the lake's catalog and nothing else

writer.description: the login croft writes the catalog with

user.description: the login croft writes the catalog with

passwordSecret.description: the NAME of the secret (.env, the shell or secretsFrom) that holds the writer login's password

reader.description: the read-only login that croft serve and every command that only reads use; it must differ from the writer's

user.description: the read-only login that croft serve and every command that only reads use; it must differ from the writer's

passwordSecret.description: the NAME of the secret that holds the read-only login's password

path.description: a local lake's SQLite catalog file, relative to the project folder, e.g. "lake/catalog.sqlite"

bucket.description: the S3-compatible bucket and folder that hold the lake's Parquet files (a lake with a Postgres catalog)

name.description: the S3-compatible bucket that holds the lake's Parquet files

folder.description: a folder of the bucket that holds NOTHING BUT this lake: DuckLake's own cleanup deletes files in it that it does not recognise

endpoint.description: host[:port] of the S3-compatible store, without a scheme, e.g. "abc123.r2.cloudflarestorage.com"

region.description: the store's region name, e.g. "us-east-1" or "auto"

urlStyle.description: how the store's addresses are written

useSsl.description: reach the store over HTTPS; false only for a store on this machine

writer.description: the bucket key croft writes with, by the names of the secrets that hold it

keyIdSecret.description: the NAME of the secret that holds the writer bucket key's id

secretKeySecret.description: the NAME of the secret that holds the writer bucket key's secret

sessionTokenSecret.description: the NAME of the secret that holds the writer key's session token, when the key is temporary

reader.description: the read-only bucket key every command that only reads uses, and croft serve, by the names of the secrets that hold it

keyIdSecret.description: the NAME of the secret that holds the read-only bucket key's id

secretKeySecret.description: the NAME of the secret that holds the read-only bucket key's secret

sessionTokenSecret.description: the NAME of the secret that holds the read-only key's session token, when the key is temporary

dataPath.description: a local lake's folder for its Parquet files, relative to the project folder, e.g. "lake/data"; it holds nothing else

notify.description: what happens when a scheduled run fails

desktop.description: desktop notification when a scheduled run fails

webhook.description: http(s) URL that receives the failure envelope of a scheduled run

concurrency.description: extractions that run at the same time in one run (1-64)

http.description: settings for ctx.http, the requests assets make

budgets.description: requests ctx.http may send to each host across runs and previews, e.g. {"api.example.com": {"perHour": 50, "perDay": 125}} (perMinute, perHour, perDay)

additionalProperties.description: the most requests to this host in any rolling minute, hour or day

serve.description: the read server, the local HTTP server apps query through

host.description: read server address; anything but loopback must sit behind HTTPS

queryTimeoutMs.description: deadline for one query over HTTP

maxConcurrent.description: queries running in DuckDB at once; the rest queue

maxBytes.description: largest result in bytes; bigger results fail with QUERY_TOO_MANY_ROWS

maxRows.description: most rows one answer carries, whatever limit asks; more fail with QUERY_TOO_MANY_ROWS

allowOrigins.description: browser origins allowed to call the read server, e.g. "http://localhost:3000"

sharedTables.description: the tables a key may read, by asset name, e.g. ["orders", "customers"]; none by default, and with none every key's query is refused (croft docs keys)

stateDir.description: state folder; croft sets it when it moves state off a synced folder

secretsFrom.description: where secrets come from besides the shell and .env (croft docs secrets)

command.description: a command, run from the project folder without a shell, that prints the secrets the shell and .env lack as KEY=value lines, e.g. ["sops", "-d", "--output-type", "dotenv", "secrets.enc.yaml"] (croft docs secrets)
